SK6022 A type name repeats the keyword the declaration already carries

class OrderClass and struct PointStruct say the same thing twice; the keyword is already there, two words to the left.

CategoryDesign
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSyntax
Needs a compilationno
Runs under --load=looseyes
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since1.3

Why

A type's kind is written in its declaration, and every tool that shows the type shows the keyword: the IDE's completion list, the hover, the go-to-definition, the diff. Repeating it in the identifier spends a word on information the reader already has, and it costs the name whatever a real noun would have contributed — OrderClass is a worse name than Order, not a more precise one. The suffix is also the first thing to go stale, because it survives the edit that makes it wrong: a class that becomes a record keeps its Class suffix until somebody notices. This is not CA1711, which is about suffixes .NET has reserved — Attribute, Collection, EventArgs. These are not reserved; they are simply empty.

Example

Instead of:

public sealed class OrderClass {
    public int Id { get; init; }
}

Write:

public sealed class Order {
    public int Id { get; init; }
}

When it does not fire

Only two suffixes, and the declaration has to agree with the one it uses. Class is reported on a class or a record (a record class is a class, and a record OrderClass is the stale suffix in its most literal form); Struct is reported on a struct or a record struct. Where the name and the keyword disagree — a class called PointStruct — the rule says nothing, because there the name is not redundant, it is wrong, and "delete the suffix" is the wrong advice for a name that lies about its kind.

⚠ `Record` is deliberately not a suffix this rule knows about, even though the proposal names it. Record was a domain noun for a row of data for decades before it was a C# keyword: LogRecord, AuditRecord, MedicalRecord, DnsRecord, ResourceRecord, ActivationRecord, ChangeRecord. There is no syntactic test that separates the noun from the redundant suffix, the noun is overwhelmingly the more common of the two, and a rule that cannot tell them apart on a word this common would be wrong far more often than right. PersonRecord goes unreported. That is the price of not reporting LogRecord, and it is worth paying.

A curated list of compound words is exempt, and it is judgement rather than measurement. The rule reads the PascalCase word immediately before the suffix, and stays silent when it is one of: Base, Sub, Super, Inner, Outer, Nested, Abstract, Sealed, Partial, Generic, Derived, Test, Master, Character, Equivalence, Storage, Business, Economy, First, Second, Weight, Size, Device, Object, Working, Worker, Ref, Readonly. Two different things are on that list. In MasterClass, CharacterClass, EquivalenceClass, StorageClass, BusinessClass and WeightClass the word "class" means category and is not about C# at all. In BaseClass, InnerClass, NestedClass, AbstractClass and TestClass the type is about a class — a fixture, a sample, a node in a tool that reads C# — so the word is the head noun rather than a suffix; TestClass in particular is MSTest's own attribute name and a term of art. ⚠ The list is incomplete by construction and always will be. English compounds are not enumerable, and a name whose last word is a real compound and is not on this list will be reported wrongly. Add a #pragma or a baseline entry; the rule ships at suggestion because that is the honest severity for a judgement of this kind.

Two mechanical guards keep the obvious noise out. The name must be longer than the suffix, so a class Class or a struct Struct in a parser or a code generator — where that is the whole subject — is never reported. And the character before the suffix must be lower-case or a digit, so the suffix has to begin a new PascalCase word after a real one; an all-caps run running into it is not a suffix boundary anyone wrote on purpose.

⚠ No fix. Renaming a type rewrites every reference to it across a solution, and Skala's fix model is a list of text edits against one file's SourceText — an edit that renamed the declaration and nothing else would produce a tree that does not build. Choosing the replacement name is a person's decision in any case; Order is usually right and is not always right.
